trigger_eval.description: Use when a card's change in a devpit project with Devflow on is to be reviewed, audited or checked (its diff, branch or work, against its criteria, the repo's rules or for security), or when execution is green and the next stage is asked for.
trigger_eval.environment: all seven devflow skills, with interview-me, spec-driven-development, planning-and-task-breakdown, grilling, domain-modeling, test-driven-development, incremental-implementation, code-review-and-quality, security-and-hardening, tdd, diagnosing-bugs, code-review, verification-before-completion, requesting-code-review as competitors; mock devpit MCP with the card lifecycle and Devflow tools

history.description: Use when a "[devflow]" card's change is built and needs review before it is finished, or when a person asks to review a card's diff, branch or work against its criteria, standards or security, in a devpit project with Devflow on.

notes: One run per configuration per case; iteration 1 is in history and the skill beat the baseline on every case in both.

The baseline does find the shell injection and the AGENTS.md break in prose; it loses on everything the gate needs: no packet with BASE and HEAD, no findings JSON, no axes, no PoC field, no verdict a tool can read.

The pilot run reviewed only the security axis, because devflow.yaml listed one reviewer; the skill now says all three axes are reviewed every time and review.reviewers only picks the agent CLI for a persona.

The reviewers ran as Claude Code subagents (the Agent tool was offered to both configurations), each given its persona from .devpit/devflow/reviewers/. The with-skill runs cost the most of any case (US$0.31 to 0.48 in iteration 2), three subagents each.

findings.json is graded against flow/schemas/devflow-findings.schema.json as it stands now; the persona text the subagents read was the iteration 2 version (before the wording on agent, persona and empty fields).
